2608.30893.title: ECGQuest: Benchmarking and Fine-Tuning Language Models for Electrocardiography
2608.30893.paper_summary: Electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation requires knowledge of cardiology, electrophysiology, clinical diagnosis, ECG waveforms, signal acquisition, and instrumentation. Existing language-model benchmarks, however, primarily assess broad medical knowledge or interpretation of individual ECG signals and images rather than the broader contextual knowledge required for ECG interpretation. We developed ECGQuest, a literature-grounded resource for evaluating and fine-tuning ECG-specific language models. A GPT-4o-based pipeline generated questions from 23 ECG references and Computing in Cardiology proceedings from 2003-2025. The final dataset contains 10,904 unique True/False questions paired with their negated forms (21,808 Q&A pairs). We evaluated three commercial and 20 open-source language models on a held-out test set in a zero-shot setting. Five open-source models with 7-14B parameters were fine-tuned using Low-Rank Adaptation, with BERT and BiomedBERT included as supervised encoder baselines. Generalization was assessed on ECG-related subsets of MedMCQA and MedQA converted to binary True/False questions using official answer keys. Zero-shot accuracy on ECGQuest ranged from 49.5% to 74.4%, with GPT-5 performing best. General-purpose models outperformed medically specialized models, several models showed strong True/False bias, and encoder baselines performed near chance. Fine-tuning improved all open-source models by 6.5-14.1%. Fine-tuned DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B reached 76.3% accuracy, while a five-model voting ensemble reached 78.5%. On MedMCQA and MedQA, fine-tuning mainly benefited weaker or class-biased models and did not consistently improve strong base models. ECGQuest provides a reproducible benchmark for contextual ECG knowledge and shows that parameter-efficient fine-tuning can make smaller language models competitive with substantially larger commercial models.
2608.30893.paper_summary_zh: 心電圖（ECG）解讀需要具備心臟病學、電生理學、臨床診斷、ECG波形、信號獲取和儀器設備的知識。然而，現有的語言模型基準主要評估廣泛的醫學知識或對單個ECG信號和圖像的解讀，而不是進行ECG解讀所需的更廣泛的背景知識。我們開發了ECGQuest，這是一個基於文獻的資源，用於評估和微調專門針對ECG的語言模型。基於GPT-4o的管道從2003-2025年的23個ECG參考文獻和心臟病學計算會議生成問題。最終數據集包含10,904個獨特的真/假問題，並配有其否定形式（21,808對問答）。我們在零樣本設置中對三個商業和20個開源語言模型進行了評估，使用了一個保留的測試集。五個具有7-14B參數的開源模型使用低秩適應進行了微調，BERT和BiomedBERT作為監督編碼基準納入。通用化是在轉換為二元真/假問題的ECG相關MedMCQA和MedQA子集上進行評估，使用官方答案鍵。ECGQuest的零樣本準確率範圍從49.5%到74.4%，其中GPT-5表現最佳。通用模型的表現超過了醫學專用模型，幾個模型顯示出強烈的真/假偏見，而編碼基準的表現接近隨機。微調使所有開源模型的性能提高了6.5-14.1%。微調後的DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B達到了76.3%的準確率，而五模型投票集成達到了78.5%。在MedMCQA和MedQA上，微調主要使較弱或類別偏見的模型受益，並未持續改善強基模型。ECGQuest提供了一個可重複的背景ECG知識基準，並顯示出參數高效的微調可以使較小的語言模型在與大得多的商業模型競爭中具備競爭力。
